claims.text: The module census and its status -- wired / island / shim / unknown -- straight off daedalus.mapping.reach.analyse's classification.
claims.why: The classification mapping is defined here (STATUS_BY_CLASS), but the actual census construction is not in this chunk.

claims.text: entrypoints, entry_kinds, importers and tests per module.
claims.why: No code in this chunk derives these fields.

claims.text: the CLI dispatch table and the HTTP route table, from the entry points.
claims.why: No code in this chunk derives these tables.

claims.text: every environment switch, where it is read, whether it is dark and whether any document mentions it, from daedalus.mapping.switches.
claims.why: No code in this chunk reads switches.

claims.text: two kinds of stale: a package this repo's own packaging metadata promises that is not on disk, and a __pycache__ whose sources are gone.
claims.why: Stale detection logic is not in this chunk; only _STALE_SKIP_DIRS and _pyproject_packages scaffolding appear.

claims.text: the packaging gap in the other direction -- a package on disk that a wheel would not contain.
claims.why: No code in this chunk computes package-on-disk vs wheel contents.

claims.text: notes -- WHY a thing is the way it is. No scanner derives that.
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS includes 'notes' and _strip_human removes it from digest projection, preserving it as human-owned.

claims.text: kind -- the semantic taxonomy (safety / orchestration / provider / memory). A path prefix is a hint, not a fact.
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS includes 'kind' and _strip_human strips it from the mechanical projection.

claims.text: name -- the human-legible name of a capability, as opposed to the file it happens to live in.
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS includes 'name' and _strip_human strips it.

claims.text: status: planned and status: baseline -- a feature that has no code yet has no evidence a scanner can read, and 'this is deliberately only a baseline' is a judgement.
claims.why: No code in this chunk handles status values 'planned' or 'baseline'.

claims.text: every feature whose surface is not Python: the web app, the VS Code extension, the crew protocol files. The reachability engine walks .py; claiming to have measured a .tsx would be a lie of scope.
claims.why: This chunk does not implement any non-Python feature handling.

claims.text: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run. Human fields live in annotations (keyed to a module, an env var or a route) and narrative_features (whole hand-written entries with no mechanical counterpart), and are merged into the output for consumers -- but the digest is computed over a projection that strips them again.
claims.why: _strip_human removes _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS including 'annotations' and 'narrative_features', and _digest computes over that projection.

claims.text: editing a note, a name or a kind is legal and does not trip the gate
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS contains those fields and _strip_human removes them from the digest projection.

claims.text: editing a status, a test list or an island entry DOES trip it, because that is the half a human is not supposed to write.
claims.why: Those fields are not in _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS nor in the human field tuples, so they remain in the digest projection.

claims.text: That is a refinement of the rule daedalus.mapping.drift._digest states for the map snapshot, where the human half is a whole top-level block. Here the human half is interleaved with the mechanical half by field, so the digest is taken over a projection instead of over a key list.
claims.why: _strip_human removes interleaved human fields from areas, env_vars, and repo_state, confirming projection-based digest.

claims.text: Annotations carry human fields ONLY. An annotation cannot set status and cannot add a module, because the failure being fixed is a hand-written file steering the work queue -- handing that same power back through a side door would be the same defect wearing a generated file's clothes.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain annotation validation logic; it only strips annotations from the digest.

claims.text: The fields a HUMAN owns on a generated record. They are merged into the output so a consumer reads one document, and stripped again before the digest so that writing them is not an integrity violation.
claims.why: FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS is defined and _strip_human removes those fields from the projection.

claims.text: Top-level keys the digest never covers: the constant note, the human blocks, the digest itself, and the two fields whose value is a function of the human blocks (unmatched_annotations) or of a clock-adjacent probe that the picker explicitly refuses to treat as staleness (repo_state.dirty).
claims.why: _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS includes 'note', 'annotations', 'narrative_features', 'unmatched_annotations', and DIGEST_KEY. However, 'repo_state.dirty' is handled separately in _strip_human by reducing repo_state to {'head': ...}.

claims.text: reach classification -> inventory status. orphan folds into island: both mean 'no entry point reaches it', and the map's own gate already merges them (drift.ISLAND_CLASSES). test modules are not features and are dropped entirely.
claims.why: STATUS_BY_CLASS maps orphan to island, but the claim about drift.ISLAND_CLASSES and test module dropping is not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: Where the mechanically-detected staleness is filed. A distinct area so a reader can tell 'the tree contradicts this repo's own metadata' from 'this module is unreachable', which want different verbs.
claims.why: METADATA_AREA is defined, but its use in staleness detection is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Directories a stale sweep must NOT descend into. Deliberately NOT the same set as reach._IGNORE_DIRS: build and __pycache__ are excluded there precisely because they are not source, and they are exactly what this sweep is looking for.
claims.why: _STALE_SKIP_DIRS is defined, but the comparison with reach._IGNORE_DIRS and the sweep logic are not in this chunk.

claims.text: The HTTP method a route handler implies. web_api dispatches on the request method by putting it in the handler's name, so this is a reading of the evidence rather than a guess -- and a handler that does not follow the convention yields "" rather than a fabricated method.
claims.why: _method_of iterates _METHOD_BY_SUFFIX and returns '' if no suffix matches, as claimed.

claims.text: Tokens inside a hand-written entrypoint string that could name a module. Starts at a letter or underscore so "/api/x" and ".claude/y" do not produce a phantom leading-punctuation token.
claims.why: _TOKEN_RE pattern starts with [A-Za-z_], so leading punctuation is not matched.

claims.text: The mechanical projection of a whole document. Everything a human is allowed to write is removed: the human top-level blocks, and the human FIELDS interleaved into the generated records. What is left is exactly what this module derives, which is exactly what a digest should be a function of.
claims.why: _strip_human removes _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS, human fields from areas, env_vars, and reduces repo_state to head only.

claims.text: A hash over the derived half only. Canonical JSON, sorted keys, so the value is a function of the content and not of the writer's key order.
claims.why: _digest uses json.dumps with sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), and hashes the UTF-8 encoding.

claims.text: Does this document's own digest still cover its own derived fields? Public for the same reason daedalus.mapping.drift.digest_ok is: any consumer that RANKS WORK out of these lists rather than rescanning has to ask this first. Ranking work out of a hand-edited census is precisely the defect this module was written to end.
claims.why: digest_ok returns False for non-mapping or __error__ docs, and compares stored digest to _digest(doc).

claims.text: The explicit [tool.setuptools] packages list, or []. A line scanner rather than a TOML parser: this module is stdlib-only across 3.10 (no tomllib), and the shape being read is one array under one known table. An unreadable or absent pyproject yields an empty list, which both detectors below read as 'no promise was made' -- never as a finding.
claims.why: The function body is cut off at the try: line; the full implementation is not visible to verify the line-scanner behaviour.

observations.what: The _strip_human function reduces repo_state to only 'head', which aligns with the comment that branch and dirty are excluded, but the comment in _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS mentions repo_state.dirty as a top-level key the digest never covers, which is slightly imprecise because it is handled by reduction, not by exclusion of the whole repo_state key.

The _pyproject_packages docstring claims 'An unreadable or absent pyproject yields an empty list' but the function body is not fully visible in this chunk; the try: block is cut off, so the except handling cannot be verified.

The module docstring claims 'the census cannot be older than the run that produced it', but this chunk only contains digest machinery, not the run logic that writes the inventory; the claim is not verifiable here.

The _METHOD_BY_SUFFIX tuple is ordered with _handle_delete first, _handle_get last; _method_of iterates in order, so a handler ending in both _handle_delete and _handle_get (impossible in practice) would return DELETE.

The _TOKEN_RE pattern allows dots, slashes, backslashes, and hyphens after the first character, which could match a token like 'foo/bar.py' as a single token; the comment says it could name a module, which is plausible.
